summaries.summary: Word embeddings are unsupervised methods for latent semantic structure, distributed representations, co-occurrence statistics, and extensions beyond text; efe provides a probabilistic perspective.
sefe extends efe to study embedding variation across groups, discovering per-group representations while sharing information to avoid lack of data.
Figure FIGREF1 shows sefe on ArXiv abstracts grouped by cs, q-fin, and nlin, illustrating field-specific similar words to 1.10intelligence.
Embedding methods use embedding and context vectors; sefe uses group-specific embedding vectors and shared context vectors to keep embeddings in the same space.
Two methods share statistical strength among embedding vectors: hierarchical modeling with a global embedding and amortization with deterministic functions, fit using stochastic optimization.
The work relates to language evolution over time and multilingual embeddings, differing by focusing on words appearing in all groups and their variations.
Contributions include sefe, hierarchical modeling and amortization, experiments on ArXiv papers, U.S. Congressional speeches, and grocery data, with sefe outperforming efe in held-out log-likelihood.
sefe builds on efe to capture semantic variations across groups by learning separate embedding vectors for each object and group.
sefe extends efe with group-specific embedding vectors and shared context vectors, with Section SECREF4 reviewing efe and Section SECREF8 presenting hierarchical structures.
Exponential family embeddings learn vector representations of objects based on their co-occurrence patterns.
A dataset is a typically sparse matrix INLINEFORM0 with columns as datapoints, rows as objects, and binary entries INLINEFORM1 for word INLINEFORM2 at location INLINEFORM3.
efe represents each object INLINEFORM0 with embedding vectors INLINEFORM1 and context vectors INLINEFORM2, requiring a context, conditional exponential family, and parameter sharing structure.

Exponential family embeddings learn representations from conditional probabilities conditioned on context observations, with context INLINEFORM0 varying by application and text using a fixed-size window.
Given context INLINEFORM0 and observations INLINEFORM1 indexed by INLINEFORM2, the distribution for INLINEFORM3 is in the exponential family, DISPLAYFORM0.
With sufficient statistics INLINEFORM0 and natural parameter INLINEFORM1, embedding vectors INLINEFORM3 and context vectors INLINEFORM4 combine to form the natural parameter, DISPLAYFORM0.
INLINEFORM0 is the link function; exponential family embeddings resemble a bank of glm, with context vectors as covariates, embedding vectors as regression coefficients, and the identity link used.
The parameter sharing structure indicates how embedding vectors are shared across observations; standard efe uses INLINEFORM0 and INLINEFORM1 for all columns of INLINEFORM2.
The efe objective sums log-conditional likelihoods from Eq. EQREF5 and adds an INLINEFORM0-regularization term over embedding and context vectors, yielding DISPLAYFORM0.
Maximizing regularized conditional likelihood is not maximum a posteriori but resembles pseudo-likelihood maximization in conditionally specified models BIBREF26, BIBREF10.
sefe models grouped data partitioned into INLINEFORM0 groups, associating each instance INLINEFORM1 with group INLINEFORM2 and learning separate embedding vectors for each group.
sefe shares context vectors across groups, INLINEFORM0, while embedding vectors are shared at the group level, INLINEFORM3, with Figure FIGREF1 showing a graphical representation.
Sharing context vectors INLINEFORM0 reduces parameters, captures group differences, unites embeddings in one space, and avoids ad-hoc alignment needed by separate models.
With INLINEFORM0 groups, sefe has INLINEFORM1 times as many embedding vectors, motivating hierarchical embedding structure and amortization using global embedding vectors INLINEFORM4.
Hierarchical embedding structure assumes each INLINEFORM0, with INLINEFORM1 a fixed hyperparameter, and replaces the efe objective in Eq. EQREF7 with DISPLAYFORM0.
The INLINEFORM0-regularization term now applies only on INLINEFORM1 and the global vectors INLINEFORM2.
Fitting the hierarchical model maximizes Eq. EQREF11 with respect to INLINEFORM0, INLINEFORM1, and INLINEFORM2 using stochastic gradient ascent, tying parameters through a common prior.

Amortization sets per-group embeddings INLINEFORM0 as deterministic functions INLINEFORM1 of global embeddings, using group-specific neural networks INLINEFORM2 with unobserved inputs estimated jointly.
Amortization can significantly reduce parameters from INLINEFORM0 to INLINEFORM4, where INLINEFORM5 is neural network parameters, while retaining group-specific flexibility.
The amortized sefe model introduces parameters INLINEFORM0 for each group INLINEFORM1, obtaining group-specific embedding vectors INLINEFORM2 as DISPLAYFORM0.
Two architectures for INLINEFORM0 are compared: fully connected feed-forward neural networks and residual networks BIBREF32, both with one hidden layer of INLINEFORM1 units.
The network parameters INLINEFORM2 are two weight matrices, DISPLAYFORM0, and the network maps global embedding vector INLINEFORM1 to group-specific embedding vectors INLINEFORM2.
Using hyperbolic tangent nonlinearity, residual networks model differences from global vectors INLINEFORM1, while zero weights yield 0 for feed-forward networks and INLINEFORM2 for residual networks.
The objective function under amortization is given by DISPLAYFORM0.
The objective is maximized with respect to INLINEFORM0, INLINEFORM1, and INLINEFORM2 using stochastic gradient ascent, with hierarchical and amortized sefe implemented in TensorFlow BIBREF33.
Structured Bernoulli embeddings for grouped text use binary matrix INLINEFORM0 and group indicators INLINEFORM1, conditional Bernoulli distributions, and negative sampling for zeros.
The context INLINEFORM0 at each position INLINEFORM1 is the set of surrounding words in the document according to a fixed-size window.
Structured Poisson embeddings model supermarket purchases by month, with rows indexing items, columns indexing shopping trips, and context INLINEFORM7 as purchased items excluding INLINEFORM9.
Poisson conditional distribution is used for count data, and Poisson sefe downweighs zeros to focus inference on positive purchase signal BIBREF10, BIBREF2.
The experimental study fits sefe on three datasets against efe BIBREF10, showing benefits from shared context vectors, amortization, and hierarchical structure.
sefe is applied to ArXiv papers, U.S. Senate speeches, and supermarket grocery shopping data, summarized in Table TABREF17.
ArXiv papers contains abstracts under 19 different tags between April 2007 and June 2015, treating each tag as a group and splitting into training, validation, and test sets.
Senate speeches contains U.S. Senate speeches from 1994 to mid 2009, grouped by state and Republican or Democratic affiliation into 83 groups.
Grocery shopping data contains purchases of INLINEFORM0 customers over 97 weeks, with INLINEFORM1 unique items at the 1.10upc level after removing low-frequency items.
For text corpora, vocabulary is fixed to the 15k most frequent terms, non-vocabulary words removed, and words downsampled with probability INLINEFORM0 based on frequency INLINEFORM1.
For text data, Bernoulli distribution is the conditional exponential family; for shopping data, Poisson distribution is used for count data.
On each dataset, four sefe-based approaches are compared with two efe BIBREF10 baselines, all fit using sgd BIBREF34.
